card.text: The hottest known giant planet, on a polar orbit around a flattened, fast-spinning star.

sources.label: Mansfield et al. 2020
sources.quote: KELT-9b is the hottest known transiting planet

sources.label: Ahlers et al. 2020
sources.quote: a rapidly rotating, oblate early-A-type star in a polar orbit

introduction.text: KELT-9b circles its star every 36 hours, passing over its poles. Its day side is about 4,600 K, as hot as a K-type star.

sources.label: Gaudi et al. 2017
sources.quote: we measure the KELT-9b's day-side temperature to be ~4600 K. This is as hot as stars of stellar type K4

temperature.title: Spitzer heat map
temperature.summary: Heat at 4.5 µm from the paper's phase-curve fit. It varies only with longitude: the data hold no north-south detail.
